proposed_fixes.title: Recognize the IPv4 loopback range in duplicate exemptions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: DuplicateService's exact-string exemption recognizes 127.0.0.1 but not 127.0.0.2 or other 127/8 addresses, even when loopback-duplicate warnings are disabled.
plan: Introduce one shared address-exemption predicate using IPAddress.TryParse and IPAddress.IsLoopback for actual loopbacks, retaining the existing explicit unspecified-address compatibility exemptions.
Use that predicate in both Initialize and SetDuplicate when LoopbackDuplicates is false; do not disable ordinary non-loopback duplicate detection.
Add focused tests for 127.0.0.1, 127.0.0.2, another 127/8 address, IPv6 loopback forms, unspecified addresses, invalid input and non-loopback controls.
Cover both initial file loading and incremental entry edits, with LoopbackDuplicates enabled and disabled.
verification: Load two distinct hostnames mapped to 127.0.0.2 with loopback duplicate warnings off; neither receives the address-duplicate warning.
Turn the setting on and verify warnings return; repeat through add/edit/reload.
Verify same-type non-loopback duplicate-host and duplicate-address rules remain unchanged.

confidence.rationale: The exact reported address and setting map directly to two inspected exact-string guards that exclude it. No environment-specific state is required for this mechanism; runtime tests remain implementation work.

inferences: A shared parsed-loopback predicate should cover the reported range mismatch without broadening exemptions to unrelated addresses.
